title: Health knocks on the Collector instead of counting Spans

statements.says: Health sends an empty payload to each of the Collector's two doors and reads the answer, instead of counting the Spans the Trace store holds.
A door that answers 404 is not wired to a store, a door that refuses the connection has no Collector behind it, and both are faults that name the action that would change them.
The Collector is a part of its own, with a Lamp of its own.
One Lamp covers both of the Collector's doors, and its Detail names the door that is shut.
Health now writes, but the write is empty and goes to the Collector, never to a store, so a health check can move nothing Studio measures.
The Trace store's own Lamp still answers for the road behind the Collector's door.
A Collector that answers but hands nothing on is invisible to every reader Studio has.
This happened: the Collector served the events door and answered 404 on the Spans door for two days while Health showed the Trace store working.
An empty payload holds no Span and no event, so it writes nothing and no figure a reader sees can move because Health asked.
The Collector was the one link in the chain nobody watched, and it is the link that broke.
Hanging the Spans door off the Trace store's Lamp is what let the fault hide behind a part that was working.
Knocking proves the door, not the road behind it, so a Collector that takes a payload and drops it further on is still invisible, which is why the Trace store keeps its own Lamp.

Counting what the Trace store holds and calling an empty store broken was rejected, because an empty store is the ordinary state of a quiet machine, a new install or anyone who has not run Claude Code today, and it measures work done, not whether the wiring holds.
